hierarchy.h1: text-5xl md:text-6xl tracking-tight font-light font-serif text-ink
hierarchy.subtitle: text-sm tracking-[0.2em] uppercase font-sans text-ink/70

surfaces.book_texture: before:content-[''] before:absolute before:inset-0 before:bg-[url('/noise.png')] before:opacity-20 before:mix-blend-overlay before:pointer-events-none

marketing_page.strategy: Editorial Tetris Grid. Heavy asymmetry. Large hero images with overlapping text blocks. Extreme whitespace.
marketing_page.spacing: py-24 md:py-32 px-6 md:px-12 gap-8 md:gap-16

editor_workspace.strategy: Fixed glassmorphism top nav, fixed left sidebar for templates/photos, absolute positioned floating right toolbar for text/photo editing. Center canvas is scrollable/pannable with the 3D book centered.
editor_workspace.canvas: bg-[#EAE9E4] min-h-screen pt-24 pb-12 px-8 flex items-center justify-center overflow-auto

motion.page_flip: Realistic CSS 3D rotation with transform-origin on the spine (left for right page, right for left page). Use react-pageflip library.
motion.hover_states: Subtle -translate-y-1 and opacity shifts. No bouncy animations. Sophisticated and calm.
motion.ai_processing: Elegant smooth fade-ins, gentle skeleton loaders, and a high-end typography-based loading screen (e.g., 'Curating your moments...').

accessibility.contrast: Ensure all text on colored book covers meets APCA / WCAG standards. The teal cover with coral/white text must have sufficient contrast.
accessibility.testing: All interactive elements MUST have data-testid attributes.

instructions_to_main_agent: Use .js and .jsx extensions exclusively. Do NOT use .tsx or .ts files.
Implement the landing page with an editorial, asymmetrical aesthetic. Use 'Cormorant Garamond' for large, impactful headings. Avoid centered, generic SaaS layouts.

Build the 6 Cover Templates feature: Allow the user to select from 6 strict color/layout themes (e.g., Teal + Coral, Sand + Forest, Navy + Gold). Each template must have a predefined typography set and layout (title on front, location map/country on back, title + date on spine).
For the photo upload: Include a bulk drag-and-drop zone. Show a highly polished 'AI analyzing and sorting photos' loading screen instead of standard spinners.
Implement the Page Editor: The book must be previewed as a 3D flipbook using 'react-pageflip' or robust CSS 3D transforms showing two pages side-by-side.
The Editor must allow dragging photos onto pages, resizing them, and adding/editing text (font family, color, size). Pages must have varied, dynamic grid layouts (not just 1 image per page).

Do NOT use standard Shadcn cards with thick borders and drop shadows for the core UI. Use flat, un-bordered elements or 1px subtle lines. The UI must feel like an invisible tool around the physical book.
Use 'data-testid' on all interactive elements (buttons, inputs, dropzones, canvas elements) to ensure robust testability.
Ensure the PDF export feature grabs the high-res DOM representation of the book for print.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
NEVER use generic purple gradients or the 'Inter' font for headings.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy, NOT by adding generic drop shadows to everything.

DO NOT use complete `transparent` background in header, overlays, any surface that has content under it. Example: Dropdown with transparent background. Use proper solid colors or backdrop blur with an opacity overlay.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition (e.g., transition: all). Always add transitions for specific interactive elements excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container in CSS. It disrupts natural reading flow.
NEVER use AI assistant Emoji characters like robot, brain, lightbulb for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable, but heavily customize them to remove the generic SaaS look.
